units.source_excerpt: Our basic model can be divided into two parts. The first part is to find a half-pipe shape which can maximize Vertical Air; in the second part, we adapt the shape to maximize the possible total angle of rotation.
units.function: Map the two official performance objectives to dependent model stages before giving details.
units.reusable_pattern: Divide the model into {n} stages; assign one decision objective to each stage and state how the later stage adapts the earlier one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim dependency unless the later model actually reuses the earlier state or geometry.

units.source_excerpt: The major assumption is that the resistance includes the friction of snow and air drag. The former is proportional to the normal force and the latter is proportional to the square of velocity.
units.function: Compress the governing physical assumptions into a paired constitutive statement.

features.clause_structure: topic sentence followed by former-latter parallelism

units.reusable_pattern: State the dominant modeling assumption, then define paired mechanisms through a {former}/{latter} contrast.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide materially different mechanisms under one generic resistance term.

units.source_excerpt: In the first part of our basic model, we obtain a differential equation of E lost based on force analysis and Energy Conservation. Then we derive the representation of E lost by solving the equation.
units.function: Walk the reader through a formula-bearing derivation-to-output sequence.
units.reusable_pattern: Move from {physical analysis} to {governing equation}, then to {solved quantity} and finally to {decision output}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the intermediate quantity that connects a governing equation to an output.

units.source_excerpt: We analyzed the effects of factors such as width, height and gradient angle of half-pipe on Vertical Air by controlling other factors, and found that wider, steeper course with proper depth and the best path are preferred.
units.function: Preview local effects, global search, hybrid objective, and practical tradeoffs in their later execution order.
units.reusable_pattern: Preview {local analysis}, {global search}, {combined objective}, and {practical constraints} in the same order used by the body.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a bounded search global without stating its feasible domain.

units.source_excerpt: We finely model the entire complicated proceeding and give numerical solution of optimal course, and establish an objective evaluating function to analyze local and global optimal course. Yet, the model hasn't provided analytic solution of optimal course.
units.function: Close with a concise product claim followed immediately by a concrete boundary.

features.voice: active first-person plural and model subject
features.clause_structure: cumulative contribution sentence plus short contrast

units.reusable_pattern: End an ambitious contribution summary with one short contrastive sentence naming the exact capability still absent.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not substitute a generic limitations sentence for the missing capability.

units.source_excerpt: A half-pipe is the venue in which gravity extreme sports such as snowboarding and skateboarding are held. It usually consists of two concave ramps, topped by copings and decks, facing each other across a transition.
units.function: Define the physical object through composition before introducing the decision problem.
units.reusable_pattern: Define {object} by category, components, and operating context before introducing symbols or optimization.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not begin with symbols before the physical object is recognizable.

units.source_excerpt: No explicit analysis of the best shape of a half-pipe is found. However, it is usually accepted that the half-pipe is 100 to 150 meters long, 17 to 19.5 meters wide and has a height of 5.4 to 6.5 meters.
units.function: Contrast a missing decision analysis with concrete descriptive practice ranges.

features.clause_structure: gap statement followed by quantitative contrast

units.reusable_pattern: Existing practice reports {descriptive ranges}, but does not determine {decision quantity}; use the contrast to motivate a model.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an exhaustive literature gap without a documented search.

units.source_excerpt: Half-pipe snowboarding is currently judged in competition using subjective measures. Still, there is strong community perception that air-time and the degree of rotation play a major role in competition success.
units.function: Turn a subjective evaluation setting into two named measurable proxies while acknowledging prior work.

features.clause_structure: problem sentence followed by concessive metric bridge

units.reusable_pattern: When evaluation is subjective, name the measurable proxies used by practice and distinguish perception from validated causation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not equate scoring correlation with causal facility performance.

units.source_excerpt: A cycle: the start of a cycle is the moment when the snowboarder reaches the edge of the half-pipe after a fly, and the end of a cycle is the next start.
units.function: Define the repeated process by observable start and end events.
units.reusable_pattern: Define a repeated unit by its observable start event and next recurrence rather than by an informal label.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave repeated-run boundaries implicit.

units.source_excerpt: Fly: the part of the movement when the snowboarder is airborne. Flying distance: the displacement along z direction during the fly. Flying time: the duration of the fly.
units.function: Build a compact family of phase, displacement, and duration definitions.
units.reusable_pattern: Define a phase, then its spatial and temporal measures in parallel clauses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use distance and displacement interchangeably without a frame.

units.source_excerpt: Figure 3 shows the definition of the coordinate variables x, y, z. Among the coordinate variables, x is the free variable, while y and z are functions of x depending on the shape of the half-pipe and path of the snowboarder.
units.function: Move from a symbol table to a geometric dependency explanation.
units.reusable_pattern: After listing symbols, state which variable is free, which are dependent, and what physical choices determine them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let a symbol table substitute for dependency semantics.

units.source_excerpt: The cross-section of the half-pipe has to be a curve which is convex downwards and second-order derivable at every point except for the endpoints.
units.function: Define the admissible geometric class before optimization and explicitly defer mechanical feasibility.
units.reusable_pattern: State geometric admissibility, name exceptions, and explicitly mark any feasibility dimension deferred to a later section.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not later call an unconstrained shape practical without reinstating deferred feasibility.

units.source_excerpt: The snowboarder keeps a crouching position during the whole course of his performance on the half-pipe, and he stands up to gain speed right at the edge before the fly.
units.function: Separate a baseline posture schedule from the later athlete-agency extension.
units.reusable_pattern: Specify the actor state during each phase and the discrete action at the phase boundary.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce later athlete choices without identifying which baseline assumptions they replace.

units.source_excerpt: The friction of the snow is proportional to the normal force, and the coefficient is alpha. Air drag is proportional to the square of velocity, and the coefficient is beta.
units.function: State two loss laws in repeated mechanism-proportionality-coefficient form.
units.reusable_pattern: For each loss mechanism, repeat the frame: {mechanism} is proportional to {driver}, with coefficient {symbol}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not mix force and work laws without units and path integration.

units.source_excerpt: A cycle can be divided into two parts. The first part is the movement on the half-pipe, and the second part is the airborne performance.
units.function: Anchor a complex mechanics model in a simple two-phase physical decomposition.
units.reusable_pattern: Partition one complete cycle into physically distinct phases before assigning equations to each.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use one balance law across phases with different forces without a handoff state.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the fact that E lost is caused by the resistance of snow and air, we can derive an equation about E lost with the help of integration after we derive the representation of resistance by force analysis.
units.function: Expose the derivation order from forces through integrated loss to terminal energy.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the mechanism, derive its local law, integrate over the path, and hand the accumulated quantity to the balance equation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the measure with respect to which a loss is integrated.

units.source_excerpt: There are three kinds of force acting on the snowboarder: gravity, normal force and resistance. Resistance includes air drag and friction between the snow and snowboard.
units.function: Introduce a force inventory before projecting and simplifying it.
units.reusable_pattern: Enumerate all modeled forces, then decompose any aggregate force into mechanisms before writing equations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce an omitted force later without revising the inventory.

units.source_excerpt: The smaller E lost, the better. So we need to find the extreme of E lost and its condition. However, since the relationship between y and x as well as that between z and x are unknown, the representation of E lost is a functional.
units.function: Convert a physical preference into an optimization target, then explain why numerical treatment is needed.

features.clause_structure: short objective sentence plus however limitation

units.reusable_pattern: State the direction of improvement, formulate the extremum, then name the mathematical obstacle that motivates the numerical method.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use numerical complexity as evidence that the chosen solver is valid.

units.source_excerpt: If we neglect the air drag during the fly, vertical air can be represented as follows. If we take the air drag during the fly into account, according to Newton Law...
units.function: Present a no-drag baseline and drag extension as an explicit paired case split.
units.reusable_pattern: Present the tractable baseline first, then introduce one additional mechanism and its changed equation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe the extension as a validation of the baseline.

units.source_excerpt: The angular momentum can be disintegrated into three directions, x, y and z. The shape of the half-pipe can only affect Lz0, while Lx0 and Ly0 are determined by the snowboarder.
units.function: Allocate response components to course design versus athlete control.
units.reusable_pattern: Decompose a vector response, assign each component to a controllable source, and optimize only the components owned by the decision variable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not optimize a component attributed entirely to an unmodeled actor.

units.source_excerpt: Given the initial angular momentum, list and explain some possible tricks: twist of beginners' level; flip and double cork; flip-twist-flip.
units.function: Translate abstract angular-momentum components into a progressive trick taxonomy.
units.reusable_pattern: After defining components, map them to domain cases from simple to combined behavior.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat an illustrative taxonomy as a calibrated trick predictor.

units.source_excerpt: Then we calculate the resulting vertical air using both analytical equations and numerical simulation. Since we can obtain vertical air, duration of fly and flying distance more easily by numerical simulation, we also use numerical simulation for later analysis.
units.function: Use the analytic case as a benchmark before selecting simulation for downstream outputs.
units.reusable_pattern: Compare analytic and numerical results on a tractable case, then state why one method is retained for the full analysis.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call analytic agreement external validation.

units.source_excerpt: Using recommended width, height, flat length and gradient angle, with other parameters fitting the reality in Snowboard half-pipe game, the resulting maximum Vertical Air is about 7 meters.
units.function: Place a model output beside an athlete-performance range as a scoped plausibility check.
units.reusable_pattern: Under {named configuration}, report {output} and compare it with {external range} as plausibility, not proof.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not label range consistency as validation without a measurement protocol.

units.source_excerpt: As to the sensitivity, we modified parameters by plus or minus 10 percent and recorded the Vertical Air change percentage.
units.function: State the perturbation rule and response measure in one compact sentence before the table.
units.reusable_pattern: Before a sensitivity table, name the perturbed inputs, perturbation size, and reported response measure.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call one-at-a-time local perturbations full model robustness.

units.source_excerpt: In the basic model above, we generally neglect the influence of the snowboarder on the flying path, but rather pay most attention to the objective factors. In this extended model, we take the impact of the snowboarder into account.
units.function: Open the extension by naming exactly what the baseline omitted and what is now added.

features.clause_structure: baseline contrast followed by extension sentence
features.transition: but; nevertheless; in this extended model

units.reusable_pattern: State what the base model held out, why it matters, and the single new influence introduced by the extension.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a qualitative addition a complete behavioral model.

units.source_excerpt: A snowboarder is different from a rigid body in that he can turn and decelerate where a small ball or a stick cannot. This means that a skilled snowboarder may move in a direction partly determined by himself.
units.function: Use a rigid-body contrast to motivate athlete-controlled path choice.
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast the idealized object with the real actor, then translate the difference into one new control variable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer an unconstrained energy redirection from the ability to steer.

units.source_excerpt: To sum up, a skilled snowboarder would choose a path with a reasonable zt and reduce his z velocity right before the fly while maintaining his y velocity, or convert part of kinetic energy in the z direction into that in the y direction.
units.function: Close a multi-factor discussion with two explicit athlete strategies.
units.reusable_pattern: Summarize a qualitative control discussion as a small set of explicit alternative actions and affected state components.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present an energy conversion as feasible without force or impulse mechanics.

units.source_excerpt: Firstly, landing on the transition part is much safer and easier than doing so at coping. Furthermore, as flying in the air avoids friction from snow, replacing part of movement on the half-pipe with an airborne one can help lessen the decrease of skiing speed.
units.function: Compare two landing choices through safety, precision, airtime, and retained-speed considerations.

features.transition: firstly; the latter; furthermore; in a word

units.reusable_pattern: Compare options criterion by criterion, preserve opposing advantages, then issue a qualified rather than universal recommendation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a landing safer without impact or contact evidence.

units.source_excerpt: We have used numerical method to test how Vertical Air is affected by other factors: width of the ramp, gradient angle of the pipe, path the snowboarder chooses, etc. Optimizing all factors, we got an optimal course cross-section.
units.function: Answer the official question first in plain language, then point to the analysis that supports it.
units.reusable_pattern: Begin each official-question section with a direct answer naming the metric, decision variables, and resulting design class.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the result optimal outside the searched domain.

units.source_excerpt: By simulating with numerical method with W varying from 10 to 25, we can find the wider the ramp is, the faster the snowboarder can speed up before the fly and, consequently, the larger Vertical Air is.
units.function: Read a paired response figure as input range, mechanism-linked outputs, and decision direction.
units.reusable_pattern: For a response plot, state the swept range, intermediate response, final response, and practical boundary.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer causation beyond the fixed simulation configuration.

units.source_excerpt: We enumerate width from 13 m to 18 m, height from 2 m to 6 m, flat length from 4 m to 6 m, zt from 0 to 15 and theta from 15 to 20 degrees.
units.function: Declare the bounded search box before reporting a selected design.
units.reusable_pattern: List every decision range and criterion before reporting a bounded optimum.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit bounds when selected values lie on them.

units.source_excerpt: Simulation results show that the duration of fly is almost positive linear to ramp width, ramp height and flat length. Duration of fly reaches locally optimum when zt is around 6 meter.
units.function: Separate monotone factor effects from a local interior optimum in one result paragraph.
units.reusable_pattern: Distinguish monotone responses from interior optima and retain qualifiers such as {approximately} and {locally}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not silently reconcile a later selected value that conflicts with the local optimum.

units.source_excerpt: It enjoys the characteristics of previous optimized shapes based on different objective functions, which may provide the eclectically best snowboard performance to certain extent.
units.function: Frame the hybrid curve as a compromise inheriting traits from two single-objective designs.

features.modality: may and to a certain extent

units.reusable_pattern: Describe a hybrid solution by the single-objective traits it retains and qualify the claimed combined benefit.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the optimized objective value as independent validation.

units.source_excerpt: Define controlling points of the curves; generate sampling points of convex curves; define gene and fitness function; run the genetic algorithm; optimize curve.
units.function: Display the optimizer as a five-stage workflow from representation to selected curve.
units.reusable_pattern: Present an optimizer as representation, feasibility generation, encoding, objective, operators, and output.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let a flowchart replace parameter, seed, and stopping-rule disclosure.

units.source_excerpt: Here we use a random method to generate convex samplings, which smoothly connect two fixed points, the coping edge and bottom edge.
units.function: State the generator purpose and its endpoint and convexity constraints before formulas.
units.reusable_pattern: Before a stochastic generator, state the object generated and every invariant it is meant to preserve.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim smoothness beyond the discrete constraints actually enforced.

units.source_excerpt: The result of Genetic Algorithm leads to the best curve, which provides maximum Vertical Air. We fit the optimistic curve as second-order differentiable curves and it ends up into an ellipse and adding a Vert about half meter long.
units.function: Move from stochastic search output to an interpretable geometric approximation.

features.clause_structure: result sentence followed by fit interpretation

units.reusable_pattern: After optimization, show the selected object, then fit a simpler interpretable family and compare it with prior design practice.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a visual fit perfect without a residual metric.

units.source_excerpt: Wider and higher ramp, larger gradient angle, theta chosen by skilled snowboarder all contribute to Vertical Air. While the width and height of the course is fixed, the shape of the course is close to an ellipse.
units.function: Close Question 1 with factor directions, conditional geometry, and small practical refinements.
units.reusable_pattern: Conclude with directional effects first, then state the shape result under its fixed conditions and practical qualifications.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the fixed dimensions when restating the shape result.

units.source_excerpt: We have tailored the shape of the course and optimize degree of rotation which correlates to following requirements respectively: optimize total duration of fly; optimize initial angular momentum along z-direction; optimize total degree of rotation.
units.function: Split the second official answer into three nested optimization targets.
units.reusable_pattern: For a compound official task, enumerate the intermediate objectives in the exact order needed to compute the final one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat separately optimized intermediates as automatically jointly optimal.

units.source_excerpt: The resulting optimum of Gene Algorithm is shown below. This curve can also be fitted with second order curve, which is an ellipse as well.
units.function: Report the total-rotation result with a figure-led shape interpretation before moving to the hybrid objective.
units.reusable_pattern: Use a compact figure-led conclusion to close one objective, then explicitly hand off to the combined objective.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the fitted family as proof that the stochastic search converged.

units.source_excerpt: What tradeoffs may be required to develop a practical course? Answer 3: radius of curvature; flat bottom; E reach; number of cycles.
units.function: Restate the practical question and immediately decompose it into four decision dimensions.
units.reusable_pattern: Turn a broad practical question into a short ordered list of constructability, safety, state-retention, and capacity criteria.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call criteria constraints unless they enter the feasible set or decision rule.

units.source_excerpt: The radius of curvature of the half-pipe cross-section cannot be too small, or the snow may fall off. Since the 1980s, half-pipes have had extended flat ground added between the quarter-pipes.
units.function: Combine a physical feasibility bound with historical design practice before discussing performance effects.

features.clause_structure: constraint clause followed by practice evidence

units.reusable_pattern: For each practical feature, pair a physical or operational reason with observed design practice and modeled performance effects.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer a safe numerical radius from qualitative statements.

units.source_excerpt: In the Winter Olympic Games, a snowboarder must perform 5 to 8 acrobatic tricks in a run. Thus, a snowboarder should complete 5 to 8 cycles in the half-pipe's 110 m extent.
units.function: Translate an event requirement into a finite-course capacity constraint and slope recommendation.
units.reusable_pattern: Convert an external count requirement and finite extent into a capacity condition before recommending a design variable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not equate one trick with one cycle without checking the event definition.

units.source_excerpt: The model describes the entire proceeding of movement in a detailed manner, which pertains to intricate correlation between many physical quantities and is well-organized.
units.function: Open self-assessment with the paper's integrated architecture rather than a generic adjective alone.
units.reusable_pattern: State a strength as a concrete retained architecture or operation, followed by why it helps the analysis.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use precise, robust, or valid without a passed criterion.

units.source_excerpt: We established an objective evaluating function to compare different shapes of courses. We analyzed local optimal course to learn the individual impact of the parameters as well as global optimal course.
units.function: Use repeated We-plus-action clauses to inventory concrete analytical capabilities.
units.reusable_pattern: Inventory strengths through repeated {we + operation + object + purpose} clauses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let repeated capability claims exceed the evidence recorded in methods and results.

units.source_excerpt: The model does not provide analytic solution of optimal course. The model does not take the detailed mechanical characteristics and the on-snow performance of snowboarders into account.
units.function: Close with two direct model-subject limitations naming absent capabilities and mechanisms.

features.clause_structure: two repeated The model does not clauses

units.reusable_pattern: Write limitations as repeated {the model does not + missing capability/mechanism} statements.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace concrete omissions with a generic more work is needed close.
